newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins consolidate after rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins consolidate after rise.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds were quoted higher on Wednesday compared with late Tuesday but dealers said they had edged down later to early morning levels on profit-taking, as operators watched U.S. Treasuries.

They added news Russia hopes to sign a deal with the London Club of bank creditors in June had caused a temporary firming, followed by a general speculative decline as the market consolidated after Monday and Tuesday's rise.
A senior Russian Finance Ministry official told Reuters on Wednesday that Russia plans to sign an agreement rescheduling debt of the former Soviet Union with the London Club by June 30.
"The market has already come to such high levels over the recent days that only a major buyer could push up prices further," a Sberbank dealer said.
Dealers said profit-taking started after prices had run into resistance at 87.70, 63.00, 44.70, 50.70 and 38.90 respectively.
"MinFins eased a little bit but nothing dramatic happened. This week the market is looking how U.S. Treasuries will perform as it has been over the last fortnight," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said.
Like other emerging debt, MinFins are sensitive to any news which would suggest a further rise in U.S. interest rates, as this would push down U.S. Treasury bond prices.
U.S. first-quarter productivity and labour cost are due at 1400 GMT on Wednesday. Jobless claims of the week ending on May 3 are to be published on Thursday.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
